title: Persist task-sync exchange progress and atomic initial-import receipts
outcome: Persist task-sync exchange progress and atomic initial-import receipts
acceptance: Existing objects stores typed binding and exchange events with a compact batch import receipt; no new SQL table, column or index and no rewriting of existing canonical records. Actor attribution, canonical request equality, competing binding activation and unresolved-operation refusal are tested.

Exchange-owned retention preserves admitted raw candidates across three or more preparation generations and retains exact Git commit bytes/OID under private refs before any later branch publication. Restart and missing-artifact tests preserve uncertainty; no recapture or replacement commit is silently substituted.

One SQLite transaction validates and imports an empty-target or exact-repeat graph and records provenance, exact source commit receipt and progress. Fault tests before/after commit prove atomicity and retry without duplicate history; dry-run creates no durable state. Existing divergent/native-target refusals remain.

Recovery detects mismatched binding, branch/profile/store basis, surviving Git state after database rewind, and unresolved publication; it preserves all sides for explicit reconciliation and never infers never-published from absence at the current remote head. Tests need only local fixtures, no network.

E1 remains an internal foundation: no user-visible fetch/merge/push workflow, shared-file or real branch/index integration, live remote enablement, relay, private/runtime-state transfer, P2 authority exception or migration. Required full gates and independent reviews cover the final tree; later slices retain their acceptance.
